title: Prefix Executability: Evaluating Tool-Using Agents Beyond Final Success
title_zh: 前缀可执行性：超越最终成功的工具使用智能体评估

paragraphs.en: Tool-use benchmarks often score agents by final task success, but terminal outcomes can obscure whether the intermediate tool-call trajectory was executable. We propose prefix executability as a trajectory-level evaluation protocol for tool-using agents. The protocol measures whether every prefix of a predicted tool-call sequence remains executable under tool schemas, state preconditions, and data dependencies, and summarizes reliability using Prefix Executability Curves (PEC), First-Error Depth (FED), Trajectory Executability Rate (TER), horizon-normalized AUC-PEC, and Recovery Rate (RR). We instantiate the protocol on stratified samples from BFCL-v3 multi-turn and ToolSandbox, and on the complete Airline/Retail base splits of τ 3 \tau^{3} -bench. We observe that outcome-only and prefix-level rankings diverge: agents whose execution is conditioned on an unverified plan often achieve higher point-estimate final success than non-plan-conditioned baselines while substantially lowering TER and AUC-PEC. These divergences are precisely the failure modes that prefix executability is designed to expose: they reveal whether apparent success rests on an executable trajectory, where invalidity first enters, and whether success follows recovery from an earlier failure. As a validation intervention, explicit pre-execution plan checking can improve executable-prefix survival while maintaining competitive terminal success. These results show that final success alone is insufficient for evaluating tool-use agents and that prefix-level executability provides an actionable reliability signal for comparing agents, diagnosing failures, and assessing validation mechanisms.
paragraphs.zh: 工具使用基准通常以最终任务成功与否为智能体打分，但终点结果可能掩盖中间的工具调用轨迹是否可执行。 我们提出前缀可执行性，作为一种针对工具使用智能体的轨迹级评估协议。 该协议衡量预测的工具调用序列的每个前缀在工具模式、状态前置条件和数据依赖下是否仍然可执行，并使用前缀可执行性曲线（PEC）、首次错误深度（FED）、轨迹可执行率（TER）、按视界归一化的 AUC-PEC 以及恢复率（RR）来汇总可靠性。 我们在来自 BFCL-v3 多轮与 ToolSandbox 的分层样本上，以及在 τ 3 \tau^{3} -bench 的完整 Airline/Retail 基础划分上实例化该协议。 我们观察到仅看结果与前缀层面的排名会出现分歧：以未经核实的计划为执行条件的智能体往往比非计划条件基线获得更高的点估计最终成功率，同时显著降低 TER 和 AUC-PEC。 这些分歧正是前缀可执行性旨在揭示的失败模式：它们表明表面的成功是否建立在可执行的轨迹之上、无效性最早在何处出现，以及成功是否源于从较早失败中的恢复。 作为一种验证干预手段，显式的执行前计划检查能够在保持有竞争力的终点成功率的同时，提高可执行前缀的存续率。 这些结果表明，仅凭最终成功不足以评估工具使用智能体，而前缀层面的可执行性为比较智能体、诊断故障和评估验证机制提供了可操作可靠性信号。

paragraphs.en: Tool-using language agents operate over APIs, user-defined tools, and interactive software environments where correctness depends on more than a final answer. A valid run must maintain an executable sequence of intermediate actions while respecting tool schemas, cross-step dependencies, and evolving environment state [ 1 , 2 , 3 , 4 ] . This requirement is especially acute in multi-turn settings, where an early invalid call can corrupt later state or force the agent into recovery behavior that is invisible to outcome-only scoring [ 3 , 4 , 5 , 6 ] . Consider a service workflow in which an agent first retrieves a record, then passes the returned identifier to update, payment, or notification tools. A later call may be syntactically well formed but non-executable if it references a stale identifier, skips a required precondition, or applies an update before the corresponding state exists; a subsequent repair can still produce the desired final state while hiding where the trajectory first became invalid.
paragraphs.zh: 使用工具的语言智能体在 API、用户自定义工具和交互式软件环境中运行，其正确性不仅取决于最终答案。 一次有效的运行必须在遵守工具模式、跨步骤依赖关系和不断变化的环境状态的前提下，维护一条可执行的中间动作序列 [ 1 , 2 , 3 , 4 ] 。 这一要求在多轮场景中尤为突出，因为早期的无效调用可能破坏后续状态，或迫使智能体进入仅依据结果评分时无法察觉的恢复行为 [ 3 , 4 , 5 , 6 ] 。 考虑一个服务工作流：智能体先检索一条记录，然后将返回的标识符传递给更新、支付或通知工具。 后续调用可能在语法上完全正确但无法执行，例如引用了过期的标识符、跳过了必需的前置条件，或在相应状态存在之前就执行更新；随后的修复仍能产生期望的最终状态，同时掩盖了轨迹最初失效的位置。

paragraphs.en: Recent evaluation work has moved beyond simple terminal accuracy. T-Eval decomposes tool use into step-wise subskills [ 7 ] ; ToolSandbox evaluates task-specified intermediate and final conditions and checks for prohibited states or events [ 4 ] ; TRAJECT-Bench scores tool selection, argument correctness, and dependency ordering over full trajectories [ 8 ] ; ToolPRMBench and AgentProcessBench assess local process quality [ 9 , 10 ] ; and procedure-aware evaluation shows that nominally successful runs can still violate task procedures [ 11 ] . TRACE adds reference-free assessment of efficiency, hallucination, and adaptivity over tool-use trajectories [ 12 ] . Robustness studies further probe query perturbations, tool-set changes, and injected execution faults [ 13 , 14 ] . These efforts make a remaining gap clear: standard metrics still rarely quantify how long a naturally generated rollout remains executable before its first invalid prefix, or how often final success is achieved only after entering a failure regime.
paragraphs.zh: 近期的评测工作已经超越了简单的最终结果准确率。 T-Eval 将工具使用分解为逐步子技能 [ 7 ]；ToolSandbox 评估任务指定的中间条件和最终条件，并检查是否出现被禁止的状态或事件 [ 4]；TRAJECT-Bench 对完整轨迹中的工具选择、参数正确性和依赖顺序进行打分 [ 8 ]；ToolPRMBench 和 AgentProcessBench 评估局部过程质量 [ 9 , 10 ]；而面向过程的评测表明，名义上成功的运行仍可能违反任务流程 [ 11 ] 。 TRACE 在工具使用轨迹上增加了无需参考的效率、幻觉和适应性评估 [ 12 ] 。 鲁棒性研究进一步探究查询扰动、工具集变化以及注入的执行故障 [ 13 , 14 ] 。 这些工作凸显了一个仍然存在的空白：标准指标仍然很少量化自然生成的 rollout 在出现第一个无效前缀之前还能保持可执行多久，也很少量化最终成功有多少次是在进入失败区间之后才实现的。

paragraphs.en: Prefix executability complements these evaluations by checking the execution feasibility of the actual emitted rollout under explicit tool and state semantics. It credits alternative executable action sequences without requiring one gold path and records first failure, survival, and recovery. Appendix A compares what prior evaluation protocols measure.

paragraphs.en: We study prefix-level executability failures : trajectory prefixes that may look plausible as text but are non-executable under the available tool schema, explicit preconditions, cross-step references, or current environment state. We argue that prefix executability is a missing reliability axis because final success and reference-trajectory match conflate three questions: how long the rollout remains valid, where validity first breaks, and whether later actions recover from the break. We therefore formalize executable prefixes and report a metric family centered on Prefix Executability Curves (PEC), First-Error Depth (FED), horizon-normalized AUC-PEC, Trajectory Executability Rate (TER), and Recovery Rate (RR). These metrics primarily diagnose reliability; when reported alongside trajectory length, latency, or monetary cost, they also support efficiency-sensitive analysis by distinguishing short, valid rollouts from long or failure-prone ones.
paragraphs.zh: 我们研究前缀级可执行性失败：这类轨迹前缀在文本上可能看起来合理，但在可用的工具模式、显式前置条件、跨步骤引用或当前环境状态之下是不可执行的。 我们认为前缀可执行性是一个缺失的可靠性维度，因为最终成功与参考轨迹匹配混淆了三个问题： rollout 能保持有效多久、有效性首次在哪里中断、以及后续动作能否从中断中恢复。 因此，我们形式化了可执行前缀，并报告一组以前缀可执行性曲线（PEC）、首次错误深度（FED）、视界归一化 AUC-PEC、轨迹可执行率（TER）和恢复率（RR）为核心的指标族。 这些指标主要用于诊断可靠性；当与轨迹长度、延迟或货币成本一同报告时，它们还能通过区分短而有效的 rollout 与长或易失败的 rollout，支持对效率敏感的分析。

paragraphs.en: These distinctions are operationally important in cost-sensitive tool use. In workflows that trigger external transactions, consume scarce resources, modify persistent state, or require human escalation, the depth of the first invalid action can determine both the cost of failure and the feasibility of recovery. Prefix executability therefore provides a practical evaluation signal for deciding not only whether an agent eventually succeeds, but also whether execution remains uninterrupted or requires recovery along the way.
paragraphs.zh: 这些区别在成本敏感的工具使用中具有重要的操作意义。 在会触发外部事务、消耗稀缺资源、修改持久状态或需要人工介入的工作流中，首个无效动作出现的深度决定了失败成本和恢复的可行性。 因此，前缀可执行性提供了一个实用的评估信号，不仅可用于判断智能体最终是否成功，还可用于判断执行过程是否保持不中断或需要中途恢复。

paragraphs.en: The paper is evaluation-first. We deliberately use a minimal Dual-Loop planner-verifier intervention only as a controlled probe: we test whether pre-execution validation improves those metrics even when final success rankings tell a different story. This framing separates the evaluation contribution from the particular intervention and lets us ask when plan conditioning helps tool use, and when it amplifies invalid intermediate structure.
paragraphs.zh: 本文以评估为先。 我们刻意采用一个极简的双循环（Dual-Loop）规划者-验证者干预，仅将其作为受控探针：我们测试执行前验证是否能改善那些指标，即使最终成功率排名呈现出不同的结论。 这一框架将评估贡献与特定干预区分开来，使我们能够追问：规划条件化何时有助于工具使用，何时又会放大无效的中间结构。

paragraphs.en: We show that outcome-only and prefix-level rankings can diverge: unverified plan conditioning can improve final success while sharply reducing executability, whereas pre-execution validation consistently improves TER, AUC-PEC, and early PEC across three LLM conditions on BFCL v3 and ToolSandbox. A representative BFCL setting illustrates the pattern: an unverified plan-conditioned executor can reach the correct terminal outcome while emitting invalid intermediate tool-call prefixes, whereas Dual-Loop preserves terminal performance while restoring prefix executability. The τ 3 \tau^{3} -bench audit further demonstrates that prefix reliability and terminal success can rank methods differently.
paragraphs.zh: 我们证明，仅结果层面的排序与前缀层面的排序可能出现分歧：未经校验的计划条件化可以在提升最终成功率的同时大幅降低可执行性，而执行前校验在 BFCL v3 与 ToolSandbox 上的三种 LLM 条件下均能持续改善 TER、AUC-PEC 和早期 PEC。 一个典型的 BFCL 设置展示了这一模式：未经校验的计划条件化执行器虽然可能到达正确的最终结果，却会发出无效的中间工具调用前缀，而双环（Dual-Loop）方法在保持最终性能的同时恢复了前缀的可执行性。 τ^{3}-bench 上的审计进一步表明，前缀可靠性与最终成功率可能对方法给出不同的排名。

paragraphs.en: Dual-Loop is included as a controlled validation intervention, not as the main architectural claim. Given the user goal, tool schema, and a compact state summary, a planner proposes a structured plan. A verifier checks tool existence, schema conformity, explicit preconditions, and variable bindings. If verification fails, the planner revises the plan using verifier feedback; once verification succeeds, the approved plan conditions a ReAct executor, which alone issues environment tool calls. Planner and verifier messages are therefore method-side computation, not benchmark tool actions, and all prefix metrics are computed on the executed tool trajectory. The intervention follows planner-executor and verifier-guided generation work, but here serves as a stress test for the evaluation protocol [ 18 , 19 , 20 , 21 , 22 ] . Appendix D gives the schematic.
paragraphs.zh: 双环作为一种受控的验证性干预被纳入，而非作为主要架构主张。 给定用户目标、工具模式（schema）和一份紧凑的状态摘要，规划器提出一个结构化计划。 验证器检查工具是否存在、模式符合性、显式前置条件以及变量绑定。 若验证失败，规划器根据验证器反馈修订计划；验证通过后，经批准的计划会条件化一个 ReAct 执行器，由该执行器独自发出环境工具调用。 因此，规划器和验证器的消息属于方法侧计算，而非基准测试的工具动作，所有前缀指标均在执行的工具轨迹上计算。 该干预遵循规划器-执行器与验证器引导生成方面的工作，但在此处用于对评估协议进行压力测试 [ 18 , 19 , 20 , 21 , 22 ] 。 附录 D 给出了示意图。

paragraphs.en: We use BFCL v3 and ToolSandbox to test multi-step function-calling correctness and stateful on-policy interaction. BFCL v3 provides multi-turn function-calling scenarios under a standardized interface, making it a test bed for schema, ordering, and cross-step dependency errors [ 3 ] . ToolSandbox adds stateful tool execution, implicit state dependencies, an on-policy user simulator, and dynamic intermediate/final milestone evaluation, making recovery after intermediate failure observable during the rollout [ 4 ] .

paragraphs.en: Both benchmarks are instrumented at the action level. For each rollout, we log whether each predicted call is executable, the first failing step, its primary error label, and whether the episode later reaches benchmark-defined task success. On BFCL v3, this requires prefix-by-prefix replay of the predicted sequence rather than scoring only the terminal trace. On ToolSandbox, we derive the same quantities from executed trajectories and benchmark-provided traces, so state transitions and downstream recovery are observed directly rather than inferred post hoc.

paragraphs.en: We compare a nested intervention ladder with four variants:
paragraphs.zh: 我们将嵌套式干预阶梯与四种变体进行比较：

paragraphs.en: ReAct : interleaved reasoning and acting without explicit plan validation [ 2 ] .
paragraphs.zh: ReAct：交错进行推理与行动，且无显式的计划验证 [ 2 ]。

paragraphs.en: Prompt Planning : a planner-first variant in which a plan is generated but not enforced during execution.
paragraphs.zh: 提示词规划（Prompt Planning）：一种规划器优先的变体，其中会生成计划，但在执行期间不强制执行该计划。

paragraphs.en: Plan-Conditioned ReAct : the generated plan is provided as an explicit control signal during execution.
paragraphs.zh: 计划条件化的 ReAct：将生成的计划作为执行过程中的显式控制信号提供给智能体。

paragraphs.en: Dual-Loop : the same plan-conditioned executor augmented with pre-execution verification.
paragraphs.zh: 双循环（Dual-Loop）：在相同的前提条件执行器基础上，增加了执行前验证的版本。

paragraphs.en: Reliable tool use is not only a question of whether an agent eventually succeeds, but whether its trajectory remains executable as it unfolds. This paper introduced prefix executability as an evaluation protocol for tool-using agents, formalizing PEC, FED, TER, AUC-PEC, and RR for variable-horizon rollouts. Across the three-benchmark audit, prefix reliability and terminal outcome provide complementary information. Validation improves prefix reliability on BFCL-v3 and ToolSandbox, while the Airline/Retail transfer audit and paired sensitivity study show that this benefit is environment-dependent. Exact identities explain how high final success can coexist with frequent prefix failure, and cost measurements expose the operational price of validation. Evaluations should therefore report uninterrupted executability, recovery, terminal success, and agent-side cost together.
paragraphs.zh: 可靠的工具使用不仅关乎智能体最终能否成功，还关乎其轨迹在展开过程中是否保持可执行。 本文提出了前缀可执行性作为一种针对使用工具的智能体的评估协议，形式化了面向可变长度 rollout 的 PEC、FED、TER、AUC-PEC 和 RR。 在三项基准的审计中，前缀可靠性与最终结果提供了互补的信息。 验证提升了 BFCL-v3 和 ToolSandbox 上的前缀可靠性，而 Airline/Retail 迁移审计与成对敏感性研究表明，这一收益依赖于具体环境。 精确的个案分析解释了高最终成功率如何能与频繁的前缀失败并存，成本测量则揭示了验证在运维上的代价。 因此，评估应当同时报告不间断可执行性、恢复情况、最终成功以及智能体侧的成本。

paragraphs.en: Although we report PEC, FED, TER, AUC-PEC, and RR as retrospective evaluation metrics over completed rollouts, the underlying executable-prefix predicate is prefix-local. When available during execution, it can be checked after each candidate tool action to support runtime monitoring, repair, replanning, or human escalation before invalid state is propagated. Aggregated over rollouts, the same signals can guide offline choices such as prompt design, validation budgets, and agent selection. These uses remain complementary to the paper’s evaluation focus: prefix executability exposes whether and where a trajectory becomes invalid, but it does not by itself certify semantic correctness, safety, privacy, or fairness. Developing closed-loop agents and deployment policies that optimize against these signals is an important direction for future work.
paragraphs.zh: 尽管我们将 PEC、FED、TER、AUC-PEC 和 RR 作为针对已完成 rollout 的回溯性评估指标进行报告，但底层的可执行前缀谓词是前缀局部的。 当其在执行过程中可用时，可以在每个候选工具动作之后对其进行检查，以便在无效状态被传播之前支持运行时监控、修复、重规划或人工升级。 在多个 rollout 上聚合后，这些相同的信号可以指导离线选择，例如提示词设计、验证预算和智能体选择。 这些用途与本文的评估重点仍然互补：前缀可执行性揭示轨迹是否以及在哪里变得无效，但它本身并不能证明语义正确性、安全性、隐私或公平性。 开发针对这些信号进行优化的闭环智能体与部署策略是未来工作的重要方向。

These constraints can prevent malformed arguments, while prefix checking additionally covers object existence, provenance, state preconditions, and transition acceptance.

paragraphs.en: Prefix-level executability can improve oversight of tool-using agents by identifying invalid API calls, unresolved dependencies, and state-precondition violations before they are obscured by final-success scores. This is most useful in workflows where tool calls modify persistent state, consume resources, trigger external actions, or require human escalation. The same diagnostics may also make autonomous tool use easier to deploy in settings with privacy, security, fairness, or service-access risks. Moreover, an executable trajectory can still be unsafe, biased, privacy-violating, or misaligned with user intent. Prefix executability should therefore be treated as one reliability signal and combined with domain-specific safety policies, privacy controls, security review, and human oversight in consequential applications.

paragraphs.en: The executability scorer is deterministic and separate from the LLM-based pre-execution verifier used by Dual-Loop. The scorer evaluates the actual emitted actions against benchmark tool and state semantics; no learned judge, human step label, or single gold action sequence is required. The Dual-Loop verifier instead examines a proposed plan before execution and may change the executor’s subsequent behavior. Its acceptance decision does not establish that the emitted trajectory is executable.
paragraphs.zh: 可执行性评分器是确定性的，并且与 Dual-Loop 所使用的基于大语言模型的执行前验证器相互独立。 该评分器根据基准测试的工具与状态语义来评估实际发出的动作；无需学习型评判器、人工步骤标注或单一的标准动作序列。 Dual-Loop 验证器则是在执行之前检查所提出的计划，并可能改变执行器后续的行为。 其接受决定并不能证明所发出的轨迹是可执行的。

In the BFCL-v3/ToolSandbox experiments, the validation loop is capped at K val = 5 K_{\mathrm{val}}=5 candidate plans. paragraphs.en: Our experiments evaluate agent rollouts rather than train or fine-tune models. All LLM inference was performed through hosted model APIs; the local machine only orchestrated benchmark execution, tool-state updates, trajectory logging, and metric computation. Model inference was served by provider-managed accelerator infrastructure behind API endpoints, so per-request GPU type, GPU count, and accelerator occupancy were not exposed to us. We therefore report local orchestration compute separately from hosted inference compute. The BFCL-v3/ToolSandbox grid contains 200 × 2 × 3 × 4 = 4,800 200\times 2\times 3\times 4=4{,}800 rollouts across two datasets, three models, and four agent variants. A CPU-only local worker is sufficient for the evaluation harness; the BFCL-v3/ToolSandbox runs used a Linux worker with 16 vCPUs and 64 GB RAM, with no local GPU allocated. Wall-clock time was dominated by remote model latency and API rate limits rather than local computation; using 16 asynchronous API-request workers, the 4,800-rollout BFCL-v3/ToolSandbox grid completed in approximately 72 hours. Offline computation of PEC, FED, TER, AUC-PEC, RR, and bootstrap confidence intervals for this grid completed in under 1 hour on the same machine.
paragraphs.zh: 我们的实验评估的是智能体推理过程，而不是训练或微调模型。 所有 LLM 推理均通过托管模型 API 完成；本地机器仅负责编排基准测试执行、工具状态更新、轨迹日志记录和指标计算。 模型推理由 API 端点背后的提供商管理的加速器基础设施提供服务，因此每次请求的 GPU 类型、GPU 数量和加速器占用情况对我们不可见。 因此，我们将本地编排计算与托管推理计算分开报告。 BFCL-v3/ToolSandbox 网格包含 200 × 2 × 3 × 4 = 4,800 200\times 2\times 3\times 4=4{,}800 次推理过程，涵盖两个数据集、三个模型和四个智能体变体。 评估框架只需一个仅含 CPU 的本地工作节点即可；BFCL-v3/ToolSandbox 运行使用的是配备 16 个 vCPU 和 64 GB 内存、且未分配本地 GPU 的 Linux 工作节点。 挂钟时间主要由远程模型延迟和 API 速率限制决定，而非本地计算；使用 16 个异步 API 请求工作线程，这个包含 4,800 次推理过程的 BFCL-v3/ToolSandbox 网格在大约 72 小时内完成。 该网格的 PEC、FED、TER、AUC-PEC、RR 以及自助法置信区间的离线计算在同一台机器上于 1 小时内完成。

sents.en: This is complete coverage of these two base splits, not of every τ 3 \tau^{3} -bench domain.
sents.zh: 这是对这两个基础划分的完整覆盖，而非对 τ 3 \tau^{3} -bench 所有领域的完整覆盖。

sents.en: Each task is evaluated once under each of the four methods and three model conditions.
sents.zh: 每个任务在四种方法和三种模型条件下各评估一次。

sents.en: All methods are evaluated on the same tasks.
sents.zh: 所有方法均在相同的任务上进行评估。

sents.en: Table F.1 pools the 164 164 tasks, assigning equal weight to each task rather than to each domain.
sents.zh: 表 F.1 将这 164 164 个任务合并在一起，对每个任务赋予相同权重，而不是对每个领域赋予相同权重。

sents.en: RR is computed over the eligible episodes in this pooled cohort.
sents.zh: RR 是在这一合并队列中的合格回合上计算的。

paragraphs.en: For TER, mean FED, AUC-PEC, and final success, the intervals are 95 % 95\% task-level percentile bootstrap intervals from 10,000 10{,}000 resamples. RR uses a two-sided 95 % 95\% Wilson interval and reports the exact number of recovery successes and eligible episodes. These intervals describe task-level variation under the fixed rollout protocol; one rollout per task does not estimate within-task variation across repeated runs. Intervals for individual methods do not quantify uncertainty in paired differences between methods. The following subsections report agent costs and a separate sensitivity study with paired method differences.
paragraphs.zh: 对于TER、平均FED、AUC-PEC和最终成功率，区间为基于10,000次重抽样的95%任务级百分位bootstrap区间。 RR使用双侧95% Wilson区间，并报告恢复成功和符合条件的回合的精确数量。 这些区间描述固定rollout协议下的任务级变异；每个任务一次rollout无法估计重复运行中的任务内变异。 单个方法的区间不能量化方法间配对差异的不确定性。 以下小节报告智能体成本，以及一项采用配对方法差异的独立敏感性研究。

paragraphs.en: Table F.2 reports mean agent token use and cumulative request latency per episode for the Airline/Retail audit. These latency values measure cumulative agent-call time rather than complete benchmark wall-clock duration.

paragraphs.en: The Dual-Loop–Plan-Conditioned contrast holds the model condition, executor, task identifiers, tool specification, decoding rule, and execution horizon fixed while adding validation and revision. Token totals should be compared within a model condition because tokenization and reasoning-token accounting differ across providers and models.
